aiIntegrations.howtoTitle: How to get an API key

gemini: Open Google AI Studio at aistudio.google.com/apikey.
Sign in with the Google account that should own the key.
Create an API key (create or select a Google Cloud project if prompted).
Copy the key once and paste it into FEC-OS. Do not email, screenshot, or commit it.
Review Gemini API pricing and data terms on ai.google.dev before enabling production traffic.
groq: Open the Groq console at console.groq.com/keys.
Sign in to the Groq account that should own the key.
Create a new API key and copy it immediately.
Paste the key into FEC-OS. Groq’s API is OpenAI-compatible at api.groq.com/openai/v1.
Confirm current model availability and rate limits in the Groq console before relying on it.
openrouter: Sign in to your OpenRouter account.
Create a key and copy it. FEC-OS sends HTTP-Referer and X-Title automatically.
Paste the key into FEC-OS. You can select openrouter/free for no-cost experiments.
Free models and routing can change; confirm terms and availability on openrouter.ai before production use.

guide.title: Purchase request practical guide
guide.subtitle: Operating steps from the E3 PR manual, mapped to FEC-OS screens.

start.title: Use this as an operating guide
start.body: Create and track purchase requests, review the queue, register vendors, and keep the audit trail complete. Save only accurate business information. Never approve your own request.
steps: Identify the request by PR number, vendor, and amount — not title alone.
Read validation messages before retrying.
Stop and confirm policy when a screen default conflicts with published rules.

roles.title: Your role controls what you can see and do
roles.body: Requester creates and follows own PRs. Duty manager is first-stage review. Branch GM / CEO / finance act on assigned DOA stages. Executives configure policy. Vendors do not use the staff dashboard.
steps: Requester / User — create and follow own PRs
Supervisor (duty manager) — first-stage review and feedback
Approver (GM / CEO / finance) — review the assigned stage
Admin / Super Admin — vendors, DOA, and system settings

workflow.title: Every PR moves through the same control path
workflow.body: Create Details, Items, Payment and Files. Assigned stages approve, reject, or request changes. Approved requests proceed to milestones and clearance. Timeline and documents remain the audit record.
steps: Submit only when totals and documents agree.
A vendor compliance warning may allow work during grace.
A blocked vendor requires the correct policy action or authorised override.

dashboard.title: Start from Purchase Requests
dashboard.body: Purchases opens the live register — the same All PRs / My Queue workspace. Status totals show pending, approved, or rejected work. Refresh if the data looks stale. The gold chip counts decisions waiting on you.
steps: Open New Request to begin a PR.
Search by title, PR number, vendor, department, requester, or purpose.
Export creates the corporate Excel/CSV report — do not send it to personal storage.
Approve on a row is a high-trust action — open the record first when context is unclear.

create.title: Create the request in four steps
create.body: Details first (title, department, purpose, project/asset, priority, vendor, overview), then items, payment structure, then files. Complete each tab so later totals have the required context.
steps: A strong title describes the purchase, not merely the supplier name.
Confirm line total = estimated exposure = payment structure.
Attach quotation, scope, or comparison with meaningful filenames.
Quick-create a vendor only when they are not already registered.

approval.title: Review the correct stage before deciding
approval.body: Open Review Request on the record. Super Admin / configure users see Universal Access; others see only the stage they can act on. Read every attachment. Enter useful feedback — especially for changes or rejection.
steps: Approve when the business need is clear and documents support the request.
Request Changes when information is missing or correctable.
Reject when the request should not proceed — state exactly what failed.

after.title: Payments follow the approved structure
after.body: Record progress against the approved milestone. Confirm delivery or acceptance evidence. Do not exceed the approved request amount. Approval authorises the request; it does not remove payment or banking controls.
steps: Keep payment status aligned with actual settlement.
Do not replace approved files silently.
Escalate bank-detail changes through the vendor review process.

vendors.title: Manage suppliers from the Vendor Ecosystem
vendors.body: Approved Directory lists registered vendors. Compliance Matrix shows document readiness. Onboarding Pipeline tracks invited vendors. Use Quick-Create from a PR or the Vendors hub. Manage Files, Compliance Cases, and Extend Grace from each vendor card.
steps: Use Invite for self-service onboarding (7-day link).
Rule Matrix publishes company and freelancer document requirements.
Legacy pending assessment is a warning — it should not hide an existing vendor.
Do not create a second vendor because an invitation is incomplete.

compliance.title: Use the gateway as the risk worklist
compliance.body: Compliance Gateway shows system health, fully secured vendors, and regulatory risk. Filter or scan vendors needing attention. Export audit only to approved storage.
steps: Read System Health and Regulatory Risk together.
Run Compliance Scan when records should be recalculated.
Open Policy Settings only with the correct authority.
A score alone is not the full decision — entity type and deadline also matter.

analytics.title: Read performance and liability in one view
analytics.body: The Intelligence Console is the analytics workspace. Select Monthly, Quarterly, or a custom period, then filter departments, projects, and vendors. A chart without its period and filters can be misleading.
steps: Department Yield compares spend by cost owner.
Vendor concentration shows reliance on suppliers.
Purpose allocation shows where demand is concentrated.
Reconcile material figures with the underlying PR records before reporting externally.

crosscheck.title: Verify these defaults before committing an action
crosscheck.body: Observed interface differences are not instructions to alter production data. Read the actual dialog every time and pause when a default conflicts with published policy.
steps: Invite Vendor says the onboarding link is 7 days.
Global Policy default grace is 15 days; open compliance case may show 14 days.
Confirm freelancer QID requirements with Super Admin before sending.
Do not assume one deadline controls every link or case.

checklists.title: Requester and reviewer checks
checklists.body: A complete PR moves faster because reviewers do not need to reconstruct the business case. When in doubt, request clarification or changes.
steps: Title and scope are specific; department, purpose, and project are correct.
Vendor identity matches the quotation; items and currency are accurate.
Required files are attached and readable; no duplicate vendor or request.
Reviewer: correct PR and stage, attachments opened, feedback is specific.

troubleshoot.title: Diagnose the screen before retrying
troubleshoot.body: If data looks missing, refresh, clear search, switch to All PRs, and check your role. If an action is blocked, read the field-level message and confirm vendor compliance and stage ownership.
steps: Do not recreate records until you confirm the original record does not exist.
Escalate policy or permission issues instead of repeating clicks.

security.title: Protect links, documents, and banking data
security.body: Use your own authenticated account. Mask banking details in screenshots. Check role, entity, and PR number before acting. Never approve only because a requester says it is urgent.
steps: Do not copy full IBAN or identity data into comments.
Do not create duplicate vendors to bypass onboarding.
Do not change compliance status merely to unblock a PR.

settings.diagnosisNeverConnected: This serial number has never contacted FEC-OS.
settings.diagnosisCommandNotCollected: Device previously contacted the server, but did not poll /iclock/getrequest during this test.
